verdicts.explanation: Material, room-temperature conductivity of ~10^-7 S/cm, unit and experimental origin are correct. The 900 °C / 16 h sintering appears in a generic EIS methods paragraph and is not stated for NSP in the results, so it should be null.
The 2.6 × 10−2 Ω−1 cm−1 at 300 °C value for the high-temperature NTP phase is explicitly attributed to earlier work [14], so literature_cited is correct and the unit and temperature match.

The paper reports 11.1 mS/cm predicted from its own MD calculations for Na3TaP2O9 at room temperature, so the computational origin, material, and value are right; Ta is a substituent in the paper, so listing it as a dopant is only a minor labelling issue.
The paper reports 12.4 mS/cm computed room-temperature conductivity for Na3VP2O9 from its own MD work, matching the record's value, unit, and computational origin.

Figure 8 text states the computed 0.27 eV activation energy and the room-temperature 1 mS/cm conductivity for Na4SnP2O9 from the paper's own simulations, so the value, origin, and activation energy are all supported.
